title: Trent on scripture
hookLine: the council confirms the full canon, and scripture with tradition

cards: "But the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them." It's among the readings the Church offers for funerals, from the Book of Wisdom.
Open some Bibles and you won't find it at all. Open others and it's there, in a section set apart. In a Catholic Bible it sits among the other books, no fence around it.
Which books belong in the Bible was one of the reformers' questions, and Trent answered it early.

teach.b: First, the list. The council didn't just say the Bible matters; it wrote out the books by name, one after another, so nobody could wonder.
Among them are Tobias, Judith, Wisdom, Ecclesiasticus, also called Sirach, Baruch, and the books of the Maccabees. Catholics call these the deuterocanonical books.
The decree speaks of them as books the Church was accustomed to read; Trent made the list official and binding.

The decree says the truth and discipline of the Gospel are found in the written books and in the unwritten traditions that came from Christ through the apostles, and the council receives both with the same reverence.
Not the Bible versus the Church, but the Bible read inside a living Church. Then, where others stand, without ranking. Protestant traditions call these same books the Apocrypha.

Some Protestant Bibles print them in a separate section, as useful reading; others leave them out. Orthodox Bibles include them as well. The disagreement is real, and it's an honest one about how the early Church read.
Trent also named the old Latin Bible, the Vulgate, as the authentic text for public reading and teaching, and called for it to be carefully printed.
The council's point was to name every book the Church reads, each one in full standing.

how: Catholic Bibles print the deuterocanonical books among the others, and readings from them, like Wisdom 3 at funerals, are part of the Mass lectionary.

games.q: you're at Trent. some say only certain books belong in the Bible. how does the council settle it?
o: write out every book by name.
games.why: the council listed the books one by one, including the deuterocanonical books, and made the list binding.

practice: If you have a Catholic Bible, open to Wisdom, chapter three, or to Sirach or Tobias, and read a few verses slowly, out loud if you can; if not, stay with today's line: the souls of the just are in the hand of God.
Let one name come to mind, someone you've lost. If you pray, place them, in your mind, in that hand.

wordCard.voice: Vulgate. The old Latin Bible that Trent named as the Church's authentic text, standing alongside the full list of books it declared canonical. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole canon. A list written out by name, so nobody had to wonder. See you tomorrow.
